newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Work restarts at Colombia's Cupiagua oil field.
newsitem.headline: Work restarts at Colombia's Cupiagua oil field.

text.p: Work at the sprawling Cupiagua oil field in Colombia's eastern plains is nearly back to normal after guerrilla violence forced a partial suspension last month, a spokesman for British Petroleum said Friday.
"There's been a gradual normalization," the spokesman said, adding that contract workers were returning to the field.

Work on four exploratory wells and two flow lines in the field, which is due to come on stream early next year, was suspended on May 23 after National Liberation Army (ELN) rebels killed at least one contract worker and injured four others while seizing and burning five buses transporting them from the field.

That attack, and the bombing of a contractor's office in the regional center of Yopal, came after the ELN, Colombia's second largest rebel force, broadcast threats against foreign oil companies and their contract workers via a local radio station.

The BP spokesman said he was unable to say what percentage of the field's total work force, estimated at about 1,000, had returned to work as of Friday morning. But he said there had been a "notable increase" in the number of workers at the site since Tuesday. The delays since May 23, coupled with standby payments to workers and security and adminstrative costs, meant a total loss to BP of about $10 million, he said.

BP operates Cupiagua and the nearby Cusiana field along with the state oil company Ecopetrol. The BP spokesman said production from Cusiana is expected to rise from 185,000 barrels per day to 300,000 bpd by the end of the year. Output from the area will increase to 500,000 bpd when Cupiagua comes on stream early next year, the spokesman said.
